claim: On the 331 exact-database-row benchmark observations, median |db - quantum| = 0.0195, 92.4% agree within 0.5 kcal/mol, 0 bit-identical rows, max gap 6.9985; learned is farther: 5.1% within 0.01, median |db - learned| = 0.1291 (6.6x the quantum median).
value_found: 331 matched observations; median |db-quantum| = 0.019502833 (claimed 0.0195); 306/331 = 92.447% within 0.5 (claimed 92.4%); 0/331 exactly equal and 0 within 1e-12 (closest gap 5.85e-5); max |db-quantum| = 6.998506931 at bond_observation_0065 (db 86.068507 vs quantum 79.07) (claimed 6.9985); 17/331 = 5.136% of learned gaps <= 0.01 (claimed 5.1%); median |db-learned| = 0.129126055 (claimed 0.1291); ratio of medians = 6.6209 (claimed 6.6x). Independently reproduced by two joins (dict lookup and pandas inner merge) with identical results.
unit: benchmark bond observation (331 of 543 rows whose exact (molecule, fragment_a, fragment_b) triple exists in the DB); metrics pooled over those 331 rows, one value per benchmark row
method: python /tmp/verify7/v7b.py and /tmp/verify7/v7e.py: own script, raw-only reads (pd.read_csv on data/source_data/bde_db_full.csv.gz and data/normalized_views/experimental_benchmark.tsv), join1 = dict over molecule\x00frag1\x00frag2 -> bde; join2 = bench.merge(db.drop_duplicates(triple), inner) -> 331 rows; then np.median/np.abs/np.quantile on db_bde minus quantum_estimate_bde_kcal_mol and learned_estimate_bde_kcal_mol. Sensitivity runs: /tmp/verify7/v7c.py (alternate units, rounding), v7d.py (verbatim-value search), v7f.py (tolerance table), v7g.py (openpyxl workbook cross-check), v7h.py (raw DB-row unit).
notes: Every reported digit reproduces to >=5 significant figures. (1) Unit sensitivity: the claim's 331-row unit is correct and unambiguous - reversed fragment order adds 0 matches; if the raw DB row unit were used instead (724 rows, because 149 of the matched triples repeat as symmetry-equivalent rows) the numbers differ (median |db-q| 0.019353, 86.05% <=0.5, median |db-l| 0.108577), so the choice of unit matters and the claim chose the right one. (2) All 28 DB triples with intra-key bde spread are outside the matched set, so duplicate rows cannot perturb the result. (3) 92.4% within 0.5 is identical for both channels (coincidence, 306/331 each); the channels differ mainly in the small-gap regime (100 vs 17 rows within 0.01). (4) Interpretation caveat: quantum is NOT bit-equal to round(db, 2) on any row (only 51/331 at 0.2-2e-10 of rounding, 0 exact) and no quantum value appears verbatim anywhere in the 484907-row DB (0/305 unique values), so 'essentially the database's own value' is an inference from proximity, not a literal identity; the median gap 0.0195 is ~4x the +/-0.005 quantization floor implied by the 2-dp storage of the quantum/learned columns and coincides with the median nearest same-molecule DB gap (0.019483). (5) The same five numbers already sit in output/results/ws5_provenance.json, so the claim is a faithful transcription of that artifact; my independent recomputation confirms it rather than merely echoing it. (6) The '6.6x' is a ratio of medians of two different statistics (|db-q| vs |db-l|), not a like-for-like variance ratio, but it is arithmetically correct (0.129126/0.019503 = 6.6209).
